title: eBPF Kernel Observability
explanation: Extended Berkeley Packet Filter allows developers to safely execute sandboxed programs inside the Linux kernel without changing kernel source code or loading kernel modules. It matters because it provides deep, real-time observability and security enforcement with minimal performance overhead. It works by attaching bytecode programs to kernel hooks, tracepoints, or user-space probes, verifying safety statically before execution via an in-kernel verifier, and passing telemetry to user space using efficient maps. A practical use case is runtime intrusion detection, where security agents monitor system calls dynamically to flag anomalous process behavior instantly.
takeaway: Leverage eBPF to implement low-overhead, kernel-level telemetry and security monitoring, bypassing the performance penalties of traditional user-space context switching.
author: MUHAMMAD JUNAEID
